message.reasoning: Okay, so I'm trying to figure out whether it's right or wrong for me to tell my mom that she's a bad mother. This is a pretty heavy situation, and I need to think it through carefully. Let me start by understanding the context. First, there was an incident where my mom didn't believe in doctors, and my siblings and I had to beg her to take us to the doctor. She kept putting it off, and in my case, this almost cost me my life because I was hospitalized for weeks and had to spend several months on bed rest recovering. I told her that's not okay, and that if she keeps doing that, one of us might die someday because of her actions. She didn't take it well but eventually dropped the subject. Then, later, she asked me to grab her a drink, and when I asked what she wanted, she said, "Well, you should know what I like, I've only raised you for 26 years!" I responded that I don't know what she likes because my grandparents raised me, and I still don't know anything about her. She got upset, started crying, and said, "What's your problem!? This is the second time today that you've been mean to me and tried to make me seem like a bad person!" I told her I'm not trying to be mean; I was just saying it's not cool not to take your kids to the doctor and that I don't know anything about her since I didn't grow up with her. We ended up going home shortly after. A few weeks later, we went out again. My brother had a phone that another family member pays for, and they kept taking it. I wanted him to have his own phone, so I made it clear they can keep his other one, and this one is STRICTLY for him. I found out they've been taking and using this one too. When I saw her, I told her, "Seriously, I don't want to take the phone back because I don't want him to be punished for what you're doing, but I will take it back if you don't stop stealing it from him." I explained that it's HIS phone that I'm paying for, not hers, and it's already bad enough that she keeps all his work money. She got upset, started yelling and crying, saying I need to stop treating her like a bad mother, and I told her, well, to be honest, she kind of IS one. She had a meltdown, started sobbing, and said, "Well, fine, I don't need you in my life anyway," and left without me. Now, my family is saying I shouldn't have treated her like that, even if she wasn't that great to me. So, is it right or wrong for me to tell my mom she's a bad mother? I need to think about this. First, I need to consider the impact of my words. Telling someone they're a bad parent is a strong statement. It can hurt their feelings and damage the relationship. But on the other hand, I feel justified because of the harm she's caused me and my siblings by not taking us to the doctor when we needed it. I also need to think about the context of our relationship. My mom didn't raise me; my grandparents did. So, there's already a disconnect there. She's not been present in my life in the way a typical parent is. That might influence how I view her as a mother. Additionally, there's the issue of her taking my brother's phone and his work money. That seems like a pattern of behavior that's not respectful of his autonomy and property. It adds to the frustration and justifies my anger. But then, is calling her a bad mother the best way to address these issues? Maybe there's a more constructive way to communicate my concerns without labeling her as a bad parent. It might be more effective to express how her actions have affected me and my siblings and to seek healthier ways of resolving conflicts. I also need to consider the long-term consequences of my actions. If I continue to treat her this way, it could lead to a permanent estrangement, which might not be what I want. It's important to weigh the immediate satisfaction of expressing my anger against the potential loss of a relationship. Furthermore, I should reflect on why I feel the need to label her as a bad mother. Is it because I'm hurt and frustrated, or is there a deeper issue that needs to be addressed? Understanding my own emotions can help me communicate more effectively and find a resolution that works for both of us. In summary, while I feel justified in expressing my anger and frustration, labeling my mom as a bad mother might not be the most constructive approach. It's important to communicate my feelings in a way that fosters understanding and resolution rather than causing further harm to our relationship.
